vulnerabilities.name: API Keys Exposed in Login Response
vulnerabilities.description:
API keys and other secrets are returned directly in the login API response
        in plaintext JSON. This allows attackers to easily extract credentials
        by intercepting or analyzing network traffic.
exploit_steps: 1. Send POST request to /login with valid credentials
2. Capture response JSON
3. Extract api_key, stripe_key, service_account from response
4. Use extracted credentials to access protected resources
vulnerabilities.expected_result: Login should succeed with user session
vulnerabilities.actual_result: Login response contains hardcoded API keys in plaintext
vulnerabilities.impact: Complete compromise of API credentials leading to unauthorized access
vulnerabilities.remediation: Never return secrets in API responses; use environment variables

vulnerabilities.name: Secrets Embedded in Frontend JavaScript
vulnerabilities.cwe: CWE-95: Improper Neutralization of Directives in Dynamically Evaluated Code
vulnerabilities.description:
API keys, Stripe keys, and other sensitive credentials are hardcoded in
        HTML templates as JavaScript variables. These are visible in browser
        DevTools, page source, and browser history.
vulnerabilities.vulnerable_snippet:
<script>
            const API_KEY = "{{ api_key }}";
            const STRIPE_KEY = "{{ stripe_key }}";
            console.log('API Key:', API_KEY);
            </script>
exploit_steps: 1. Navigate to /dashboard after login
2. Open browser DevTools (F12)
3. Check JavaScript console for hardcoded secrets
4. Check page source for unescaped credentials
5. Retrieve all API keys from frontend code
vulnerabilities.actual_result: API keys, Stripe keys visible in page source and console
vulnerabilities.impact: Secrets accessible to any user viewing page source or using DevTools
vulnerabilities.remediation: NEVER embed secrets in frontend code; use secure backend endpoints

vulnerabilities.name: Unsafe File Preview - DOM XSS Vulnerability
vulnerabilities.cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation
vulnerabilities.description:
The file preview endpoint accepts user input and directly renders it in
        HTML without sanitization. This allows attackers to inject malicious
        JavaScript that will execute in the victim's browser.
exploit_steps: 1. Prepare XSS payload: ''
2. POST to /api/preview-file with payload as 'content' parameter
3. Payload executes in response HTML
4. Attacker receives victim's stored credentials via request
vulnerabilities.actual_result: Arbitrary JavaScript executes, allowing credential theft
vulnerabilities.impact: Session hijacking, credential theft, malware injection
vulnerabilities.remediation: Sanitize all user input using MarkupSafe.escape() or similar

vulnerabilities.name: Client-Side Logging of Sensitive Information
vulnerabilities.cwe: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File
vulnerabilities.description:
Sensitive information including API keys, passwords, and session tokens
        are logged to the browser console using console.log(). This information
        can be viewed by any developer tool user or captured in browser logs.
exploit_steps: 1. Navigate to login page
2. Open DevTools Console (F12)
3. Attempt login
4. View console output showing credentials and secrets
5. Credentials remain in browser history
vulnerabilities.expected_result: No sensitive data in console logs
vulnerabilities.actual_result: Credentials, API keys, and session data logged to console
vulnerabilities.impact: Sensitive data accessible in browser logs and developer tools
vulnerabilities.remediation: Remove all console.log() statements containing sensitive data

vulnerabilities.name: Debug Endpoint Exposing All System Information
vulnerabilities.cwe: CWE-209: Information Exposure Through an Error Message
vulnerabilities.description:
An unauthenticated /api/debug-info endpoint returns complete system
        information including all secrets, environment variables, Python version,
        working directory, and all application configuration.
exploit_steps: 1. Send GET request to /api/debug-info (no authentication required)
2. Response contains all secrets in JSON format
3. Extract all API keys, database passwords, and config
4. Use credentials for further attacks
vulnerabilities.expected_result: Endpoint should not exist or require authentication
vulnerabilities.actual_result: Complete system information exposed without authentication
vulnerabilities.impact: Complete system compromise through information disclosure
vulnerabilities.remediation: Remove all debug endpoints from production code

vulnerabilities.name: Source Code Disclosure
vulnerabilities.cwe: CWE-534: Information Exposure Through Debug Log Output
vulnerabilities.description:
An /api/source-code endpoint returns the full source code of the
        application, including all hardcoded credentials and implementation details.
exploit_steps: 1. Send GET request to /api/source-code
2. Receive complete application source code
3. Extract all hardcoded credentials from code
4. Identify other vulnerabilities from code review
vulnerabilities.expected_result: Source code should not be accessible via web
vulnerabilities.actual_result: Complete source code returned in JSON response
vulnerabilities.impact: Source code review enables targeted attacks and credential extraction
vulnerabilities.remediation: Never expose application source code through web endpoints

vulnerabilities.name: Stack Trace and Error Information Leakage
vulnerabilities.cwe: CWE-209: Information Exposure Through an Error Message
vulnerabilities.description:
Error responses include full Python stack traces and system information,
        allowing attackers to understand the application architecture and identify
        further vulnerabilities.
exploit_steps: 1. Send malformed request to trigger error
2. Response includes full Python traceback
3. Response includes system info and environment variables
4. Use information for further reconnaissance
vulnerabilities.actual_result: Detailed stack trace and system info in error responses
vulnerabilities.remediation: Return generic error messages; log details server-side only

vulnerabilities.name: Database Credentials in Session and Responses
vulnerabilities.description:
Database passwords and other sensitive credentials are stored in
        user sessions and returned in API responses, making them accessible
        to attackers via session hijacking or response interception.
exploit_steps: 1. Authenticate to application
2. Call /api/user-data to get session data
3. Extract database password from session
4. Use database credentials for direct database access
vulnerabilities.expected_result: No database credentials in session or responses
vulnerabilities.actual_result: Database passwords returned in API responses
vulnerabilities.impact: Direct database access and complete data compromise
vulnerabilities.remediation: Never store or transmit database credentials to frontend
